label: ka-2
title: 〜か
meaning: whether, the question of (sub sentence question)
meaning_example: Regardless of whether I had written it...

notes.text:
ka (to)

The verb of the main sentence is a question or knowledge verb.
notes.html:
ka (to)
The verb of the main sentence is a question or knowledge verb.

examples.japanese: 私が書いたかを問わず、(全て）「作者：あまつか」です。
examples.body_text:
私が書いたかを問わず、(全て）「作者：あまつか」です。 

		Regardless of 
		whether 
		I had written it or not it's (always) "Author : Amatuka".
examples.body_html:
私が書いたかを問わず、(全て）「作者：あまつか」です。 
Regardless of whether I had written it or not it's (always) "Author : Amatuka".

examples.japanese: おまえは・・・・俺が誰か知ってるのか。
examples.body_text:
おまえは・・・・俺が誰か知ってるのか。 

		You ... Don't you know who I am? [Lit: Do you know who I am?]
examples.body_html:
おまえは・・・・俺が誰か知ってるのか。 
You ... Don't you know who I am? [Lit: Do you know who I am?]

examples.japanese: 今度の出張はいつかまだ分かりません。
examples.body_text:
今度の出張はいつかまだ分かりません。 

		Regarding my next business trip, I still don't know when it's going to be.
examples.body_html:
今度の出張はいつかまだ分かりません。 
Regarding my next business trip, I still don't know when it's going to be.

examples.japanese: Please tell me who you went out with.
examples.body_text:
Please tell me who you went out with. 

		誰が一緒に出掛けたか教えてください。
examples.body_html:
Please tell me who you went out with. 
誰が一緒に出掛けたか教えてください。

examples.japanese: 書類どこにあるか(と)聞きました。
examples.body_text:
書類どこにあるか(と)聞きました。 

		I asked, where the documents are.
examples.body_html:
書類どこにあるか(と)聞きました。  
I asked, where the documents are.

examples.japanese: 飛行機がいつ到着するかわからない。
examples.body_text:
飛行機がいつ到着するかわからない。 

		I don't know when the airplane arrives.
examples.body_html:
飛行機がいつ到着するかわからない。 
I don't know when the airplane arrives.

examples.japanese: 友達にどんなプレゼントがいいか尋ねた。
examples.body_text:
友達にどんなプレゼントがいいか尋ねた。 

		I asked my friend what kind of present she wants to have.
examples.body_html:
友達にどんなプレゼントがいいか尋ねた。 
I asked my friend what kind of present she wants to have.

comments.text:
Incidently, if that was  

誰か 【だれか】 (n) (uk) someone; somebody; (P)

then I guess the translation would be 

"You ... Do you know I'm somebody?"  So I'm fairly confident it's '誰' + this 'か' rather than the usual '誰か'.
comments.html:
Incidently, if that was
誰か 【だれか】 (n) (uk) someone; somebody; (P)
then I guess the translation would be
"You ... Do you know I'm somebody?" So I'm fairly confident it's '誰' + this 'か' rather than the usual '誰か'.

comments.text: the grammar 「か」itself is a level 3, but these examples include many other grammar items (お問わずetc). maybe difficult for people at level3.
